page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 26.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1d, 0.25 MB L2, and 45 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n1-highmem-4 exhibits lower-tier processing and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (1109.89) and multi-core (2914.17) CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.39 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, which also rank in the bottom 25%. Computational benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (924.0) and image processing (1887.0), register in the bottom 10%, reflecting the older architectural generation of the Intel Xeon processor. Static web serving throughput is measured at 2.82 GB/sec, and LLM inference for a small 135M model achieves 61.37 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-4 offers a higher memory-to-vCPU ratio than standard general-purpose instances, making it a candidate for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. However, the tradeoff is a significant reduction in compute efficiency per resource unit, as evidenced by its weak benchmark scores across database operations (1173.0 in Passmark) and software compilation (2719.0 in Geekbench). This instance is best suited for legacy enterprise applications, small-scale databases, caching layers, or memory-intensive background utilities where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
